title: Thai Salmon Salad
subtitle: Sashimi-grade salmon with lime, chilli, herbs, and green papaya
excerpt: This is a Thai-inspired raw salmon salad dressed with lime, fish sauce, and palm sugar. Use the freshest salmon you can find. The acid from the lime firms the fish slightly but this is not a ceviche: serve it immediately.
sourceNotes: Raw fish salads dressed with citrus and fish sauce appear across Southeast Asia, from Thai yam pla to Vietnamese goi ca. This version draws on the Thai tradition with green papaya for crunch.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Prepare the dressing and julienne the papaya up to 2 hours ahead. Dress the salmon only when ready to serve.

content.text: This dish requires sashimi-grade salmon: fish that has been handled with raw consumption in mind. Ask your fishmonger specifically for sashimi-grade, or buy from a trusted fishmonger on the day. Keep the fish very cold until the moment you serve.
Make the dressing: combine the lime juice, fish sauce, dissolved palm sugar, chilli, garlic, and ginger. Taste and adjust the balance. It should be bright, salty, and a little sweet.
Julienne the green papaya finely. Place in a bowl of cold water for 5 minutes to keep it crisp, then drain through the sieve.
Slice the salmon as thinly as possible across the grain. Keep it on a chilled plate until ready to serve.
Just before serving, arrange the salmon slices across four plates. Scatter the drained papaya, spring onion, coriander, and mint over the top.
Spoon the dressing over each plate. Serve immediately.

items.symptom: The salmon is turning grey and looks cooked by the dressing.
items.cause: The dressing was added too early and the acid is denaturing the proteins.
items.fix: Dress at the very last second; carry plates straight to the table.

items.cause: The fish sauce-to-lime ratio is off.
items.fix: Add more lime juice and a little palm sugar to balance it.
A longer soak in cold salted water for 15 minutes draws out bitterness.
